newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD DOWNHILL CHAMPION LINDH RETIRES.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WORLD DOWNHILL CHAMPION LINDH RETIRES.

text.p: World downhill champion Hilary Lindh, one of the most decorated skiers in U.S. alpine history, announced her retirement from racing on Thursday.
"The time is right," the 27-year-old from Juneau, Alaska, told a news conference at the World Cup Finals.

Lindh, a three-time Olympian who won silver in downhill at the 1992 Winter Games and downhill bronze at the 1996 world championships, also won three U.S. titles and the 1986 world junior championships crown at the age of 16.
Lindh finished ninth Wednesday in her final World Cup race, the last downhill of the 1997 season.

"I have so many memories of Vail that I almost can't count them," said Lindh, who won her first World Cup points in Vail by finishing 13th in a downhill in 1986. A month earlier she had won the U.S. downhill title and then the gold at the world junior championships in Bad Kleinkirchheim, Austria.
U.S. skiing vice president Paul Major said: "There isn't much that Hilary's missed in her career and we're going to miss her. She had a tenacity that you must have to be a champion."
Lindh plans to compete next week at the U.S. Alpine championships in Sugarloaf, Maine, and then return to her home in Park City, Utah and continue her education at the University of Utah.
